NDIA-ICT-TPP-001
1. Governance, scope and decision rights
Statutory accountability and portfolio governance

NDIA must govern ICT technology portfolio planning under approved decision rights that support NDIA's statutory functions, responsible use of public resources and enterprise security governance, with Accountable Authority, CISO, Board or delegate involvement for decisions that create material risk, involve critical technology or require government reporting.
Applies to all ICT portfolio planning, investment, sourcing, lifecycle and rationalisation decisions.

NDIA-ICT-TPP-002
2. Portfolio planning cycle and capability roadmaps
Annual planning, capability alignment and roadmaps

NDIA must maintain an integrated ICT portfolio plan and capability roadmaps that are refreshed at least annually and whenever the operating context materially changes, showing current and target capabilities, transition states, dependencies, risks, constraints, funding needs, security actions, planned retirements and alignment to NDIA corporate objectives.
Applies to annual portfolio planning, roadmap refresh, investment intake and material technology change.

3. Authoritative portfolio register and asset metadata
Application portfolio management and asset inventory

NDIA must maintain an authoritative portfolio register for applications, systems, services, cloud and SaaS, data platforms, internet-facing assets and records-bearing systems, with accountable owners, classifications, authorisation status, exposure, support status, risk treatments, control status, costs, dependencies and lifecycle dates.
Applies to all material ICT assets, services, platforms and portfolio data used for planning or assurance.

4. Portfolio risk, technical debt and remediation
Risk appetite, ownership, exceptions and technical debt

Portfolio decisions must apply NDIA's risk appetite and security tolerance, assign each material ICT risk to an accountable owner, and use funded treatment plans to manage technical debt, unsupported technology, obsolescence, prohibited technologies, exceptions and compensating controls until risk is remediated, retired or formally accepted.
Applies to risk-based prioritisation, technical debt, unsupported assets, waivers, exceptions and urgent remediation directions.

5. Investment, budget, benefits and assurance gates
Business cases, funding, benefits and investment assurance

Material ICT initiatives must pass portfolio investment gates that test strategic alignment, options analysis, whole-of-life cost, Budget and MYEFO impacts, value-for-money, DTA engagement where required, delivery assurance, measurable benefits, benefit owners and evidence for realised outcomes.
Applies to new ICT initiatives, material renewals, business cases, Budget proposals and funded portfolio changes.

Standards catalogue, approved technology catalogue and reuse

NDIA must use approved architecture and technology standards, including Australian Government Architecture, Commonwealth Technology Standard, ISM and NDIA patterns, to maintain an approved technology catalogue, prevent prohibited or non-compliant products, prefer reuse and open standards, require approved cryptography where applicable and record approved exceptions before introduction, renewal or extension.
Applies before introducing, renewing, extending or materially changing applications, platforms, products, web services or cryptographic capabilities.

7. Secure technology lifecycle and cyber resilience
ISM, Essential Eight, authorisation, access and cyber controls

No technology asset may be introduced, materially changed or operated unless portfolio governance confirms that applicable ISM, Essential Eight, authorisation, access control, MFA, privileged access, patching, backup, hardening, protective DNS, vulnerability, threat-intelligence, continuity, recovery and breach-readiness requirements are implemented or covered by approved remediation and residual risk acceptance.
Applies throughout the technology lifecycle for applications, systems, infrastructure, managed services and services handling personal or sensitive information.

8. Supplier, sourcing, procurement and third-party assurance
Sourcing strategy, contracts, supplier risk and assurance

ICT sourcing and supplier decisions must assess build, buy, reuse, SaaS and managed-service options using value-for-money, security, privacy, accessibility, interoperability and exit criteria, and must include contract controls for supplier compliance, assurance evidence, incidents, subcontractors, foreign ownership or control risk, performance and transition.
Applies to ICT procurements, renewals, outsourced services, panels, managed services, supplier changes and contract exits.

Cloud, data centre, gateway, facility and zone assurance

Cloud, SaaS, hosting, gateway, data centre and facility decisions must be approved using security-zone, classification, aggregation risk, IRAP or ASD assessment, certified provider, physical security, resilience, cost, interoperability, sustainability, continuity and exit requirements before selection, renewal or operational use.
Applies to cloud, SaaS, managed hosting, gateways, Secure Service Edge, data centres, facilities and security-zone-dependent technology assets.
